instituteName: National Centre for Antarctic and Ocean Research
location: Bharati station is located in Larsemann Hills, Princess Elizabeth Land, East Antarctica.
history: Bharati station was inaugurated in 2012. It is India's third Antarctic research station. The station is composed of a main building, laboratories, a power plant building, a fuel platform, and a helipad. The station is located at the Historic Sites and Monuments (HSM) 60.
scienceDisciplines: Atmospheric chemistry and physics, Climate change, Environmental sciences, Geology, Geomorphology, Geophysics, Glaciology, Human biology, Isotopic chemistry, Mapping, Paleolimnology, Sedimentology.
features: Bird colonies, Bluff, Clear air zone, Coast, Fjord, Hill, Lake, Other Biological, Rock, Sea, Sea ice, Shoreline, Snow.
biodiversity: The station is located in an ice-free area. The vegetation is scarce, with only mosses and lichens being present. The fauna is also scarce, with only a few species of birds and seals being present in the area.
generalResearch: The station hosts research campaigns related to glaciology, marine biology, atmospheric sciences, and environmental sciences. Other studies are made using remotely operated devices (ROV) and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUV).

instituteName: National Centre for Antarctic & Ocean Research
location: Maitri station is situated on an ice free, rocky area on the Schirmacher Oasis in the central Dronning Maud Land region of East Antarctica.
history: Since 1983 the Indian scientific endeavors in Antarctica have been sustained on a year round basis, from the Indian permanent stations 'Dakshin Gangotri (1983-1989) and 'Maitri' (1989-present). In the year 1986, an ice free, rocky area on the Schirmacher Oasis was selected to build the second research station 'Maitri'. It is an inland station at an elevation of about 117 m and about 100 km from the sea with an Intervening ice shelf in between. Dakshin Gangotri station was decommissioned in 1990.
scienceDisciplines: Atmospheric chemistry and physics, Climate change, Environmental sciences, Geodesy, Geology, Geomorphology, Geophysics, Glaciology, Isotopic chemistry, Mapping, Paleolimnology, Sedimentology.
features: Bird colonies, Clear air zone, Hill, Ice cap or glacier, Ice shelf, Ice tongue, Lake, Melt streams, Moraine, Mountain, Other Biological, Permanent snowpatches, Rock, Snow, Valley.
biodiversity: Ice-free ground: petrels, skua and penguins are occasionally seen.
generalResearch: The infrastructure available at the station has enabled the scientists to conduct research in various disciplines such as Atmospheric Sciences & Meteorology, Earth Sciences including Glaciology, Human Biology, Medicine, Biology and Environmental Sciences.

instituteName: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR)
location: Maitri II is India's upcoming fourth Antarctic research station, planned in the Schirmacher Oasis region near the existing Maitri station. It is being designed for renewable energy and automated remote telemetry.
history: Announced to replace the aging Maitri station, which has exceeded its design life. Maitri II will run on solar power in summer and wind energy, with automated instruments relaying data to mainland India even when unmanned.
